history.dynasty: Temple relocated during Portuguese rule; present structure rebuilt over centuries
history.period: Original temple at Calangute (Bardez); shifted to Nanoda/Nanora, Bicholim taluka, in the 17th century; modern temple 17th century; marble renovation in the 1990s (verify exact dates)
history.summary: Hindu temple at Nanoda (Nanora) village, Bicholim taluka, dedicated to Shantadurga, the goddess who mediates between Vishnu and Shiva (legend: she placed Vishnu on her right hand and Shiva on her left to end their battle; depicted holding a serpent in each hand). Worshipped here as Vishweshwari; colloquially 'Santeri'. The 800+-year-old idol in the sanctum is in lingam form (verify age claim). The original temple stood at Calangute, Bardez; in the 17th century, during the Portuguese-era forced conversions, the deity was moved to Nanora, where the modern temple (17th century) was built; it was reclad as a marble 'masterpiece' in the 1990s. The temple has a Dipa Stambha and agrashalas (guest houses); the main priest is traditionally from the Bhuskute family (Kokanstha Brahmins). IDENTIFICATION NOTE: the CSV name 'Shantadurga Temple, Bicholim' is ambiguous — Bicholim has no Shantadurga temple of this name in the town proper; the prominent Shantadurga temple in Bicholim taluka is the Kalangutkarin Devasthan at Nanoda/Nanora (Nanora lies between Assonora and Mulgaon, east of it Bicholim town), distinct from the famous Shanta Durga temple at Kavlem (Ponda). Chosen identity documented as provisional. CSV NOTE: 'state' column wrongly holds the town name; actual state is Goa; CSV town 'Bicholim' is the taluka/HQ, not the village (Nanoda ~5–7 km from Bicholim town — verify). Opening hours not found in sources (verify locally). Coordinates from Wikipedia (approximate, verify).

name: Shantadurga Temple, Bicholim
town_description: Nanoda (Nanora) is a village in Bicholim taluka, North Goa, lying between Assonora and Mulgaon east of Bicholim town. Like Mulgaon, it became a refuge in the 17th century for temples and deities relocated from Portuguese-held Bardez and Salcete; several important Goan temples cluster in this belt.
